title: Subscription Management — Service
description: RED metrics, .NET runtime, Npgsql pool, PostgreSQL/Redis server, traces and logs (Aspire AppHost).

targets.expr: (sum(rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job="$job", instance=~"$instance", http_route=~"$route", http_route!~"/health.*", http_response_status_code=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / sum(rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job="$job", instance=~"$instance", http_route=~"$route", http_route!~"/health.*"}[$__rate_interval]))

(sum(rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job="$job", instance=~"$instance", http_route=~"$route", http_route!~"/health.*", http_response_status_code=~"4.."}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / sum(rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job="$job", instance=~"$instance", http_route=~"$route", http_route!~"/health.*"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Unhandled exceptions/s (ASP.NET Core)
panels.description: Exceptions that reached the exception handler (rendered as 500 problem+json).

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Share of all cores available to the process.

panels.title: GC pause time
panels.description: Fraction of wall-clock time the runtime was paused for GC.

panels.title: Thread pool
panels.description: A growing queue with a flat thread count means thread-pool starvation (sync-over-async, blocking I/O).

panels.title: Pool connections
panels.description: 'used' reaching 'max pool size' means requests queue for a connection (see pending).

panels.title: Pending connection requests
panels.description: Requests waiting for a free pooled connection.

panels.title: Connections (all databases) vs max_connections
panels.description: Server-wide: hitting max_connections fails new connections with 53300 'too many clients already'.

panels.title: Rows/s
panels.description: 'returned' far above 'fetched' points at sequential scans.

panels.title: Export failures/s
panels.description: Anything above zero means a backend (Aspire dashboard, Tempo, Prometheus, Loki) rejected or could not receive data.

panels.title: Exporter queue usage
panels.description: A queue near 100% drops data for that backend only. The Aspire dashboard ingests slower than Tempo, so under heavy load it is the first to fall behind; Tempo keeps every trace.

panels.title: Backlog
panels.description: Messages ready + unacked in all queues.

panels.title: Published/s
panels.description: Messages received from publishers.

panels.title: Acked/s
panels.description: Messages consumers finished handling.

panels.title: Consumers
panels.description: Registered consumers; 2 per queue with two replicas of each service.

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Open client connections (every service instance holds a few).

panels.title: Resource alarms
panels.description: The broker blocks publishers while its memory or free-disk watermark alarm is on.

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description: Published (received from producers), delivered to consumers, acknowledged and redelivered messages per second, all queues together.

panels.title: Connections · channels · consumers
panels.description: Client connections, channels and consumers. A drop in consumers while the backlog grows means a service lost its broker connection.

panels.title: Backlog by queue
panels.description: Ready + unacked messages per queue.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Resident memory of the broker process.

panels.title: Disk free
panels.description: Free disk space for the broker versus the limit below which its disk alarm blocks publishers.

panels.title: File descriptors · Erlang processes
panels.description: Share of the open file descriptors and Erlang processes in use; both are hard limits of the broker.

panels.title: Clients active
panels.description: Clients with a server connection (inside a transaction) right now.

panels.title: Clients waiting
panels.description: Clients queued for a server connection. Above 0 for long means PgBouncer:PoolSize is too small for the write rate × transaction time (a commit keeps its server connection until the WAL is flushed).

panels.title: Pool in use
panels.description: Server connections in use ÷ the pool size (PgBouncer:PoolSize). Close to 100% = the pool is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Queries/s
panels.description: Queries PgBouncer forwarded to PostgreSQL.

panels.title: Transactions/s
panels.description: Transactions PgBouncer forwarded to PostgreSQL.

panels.title: Longest wait
panels.description: Age of the oldest client still waiting for a server connection.

panels.title: Client connections
panels.description: Clients connected to PgBouncer by state, against max_client_conn. The API holds up to Api:PostgresMaxPoolSize connections per instance here; only the active ones cost a PostgreSQL connection.

panels.title: Server connections vs pool size
panels.description: PgBouncer's connections to PostgreSQL: active (running a transaction), idle (ready), used (released, being checked) and the configured pool size.

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description: Queries and transactions per second forwarded to PostgreSQL.

panels.title: Time per query · transaction · wait
panels.description: Average server time per query, average time a server connection stays in a transaction, and the average wait a client spent for a server connection. Wait rising while the others stay flat = pool too small; the others rising = PostgreSQL is slower.

panels.title: Traffic
panels.description: Bytes received from clients and sent back through PgBouncer.

panels.title: Standbys streaming
panels.description: Standbys currently streaming WAL from the primary (pg_stat_replication). 2 expected (Postgres:Standbys).

panels.title: Max lag (bytes)
panels.description: WAL the slowest standby has not replayed yet.

panels.title: Max lag (seconds)
panels.description: Replay lag of the slowest standby (from the standbys' own exporters).

panels.title: Standbys up
panels.description: Standby exporters that can reach their PostgreSQL.

panels.title: WAL on the primary
panels.description: Size of the primary's pg_wal directory (it keeps wal_keep_size for lagging standbys).

panels.title: WAL generated/s
panels.description: WAL the primary writes per second: what every standby has to receive and replay.

panels.title: Replication lag by standby (bytes)
panels.description: WAL still to be replayed on each standby (primary position − replay position), per standby address. Grows under write load, returns to 0 when it catches up.

panels.title: Replay lag by standby (seconds)
panels.description: How far behind the primary each standby is in time, and how long ago it last replayed a transaction, from the standbys' exporters.

panels.title: Standby state
panels.description: Whether each standby's PostgreSQL is reachable (pg_up) and in recovery (1 = a standby; 0 would mean it was promoted).
